title: Find a missing whole-number division value
intro: The dividend is made from complete groups and any leftover amount. This relationship also solves an equation with one missing value.
html:
Find a missing whole-number division value

The dividend is made from complete groups and any leftover amount. This relationship also solves an equation with one missing value.

If there is no remainder, dividend = divisor × quotient. With a remainder, add it after multiplying. A remainder is always nonnegative and smaller than the divisor.

A method to try

  1. Identify the blank and any stated remainder.
  2. Use the multiplication relationship to find the missing value.
  3. Check the entire original equation and the remainder condition.

Worked examples

□ ÷ 35 = 1404 R 21

Multiply 35 by 1404, then add the 21 left over.

□ = 49161

Check: 49161 ÷ 35 = 1404 R 21.

840 ÷ □ = 24

Find the number that multiplies 24 to make 840.

□ = 35

Check: 35 × 24 = 840.

A mistake to watch for

A missing divisor is not dividend × quotient. Divide the amount used in full groups by the quotient.

Check and explain

If the blank is the quotient, carry out division and record any requested remainder.
examples: Multiply 35 by 1404, then add the 21 left over.
Find the number that multiplies 24 to make 840.
